title: Microsoft Teams: keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls
summary: Hold: the consent-setting navigation omits the documented Edit step, and the sources do not establish the blanket identity, permission and disabled-policy recording claims. The roadmap and Message Center details are accurate, but the briefing should also acknowledge conflicting Learn guidance and include its audit recommendation in the controls table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans keypad-based recording and transcription consent for PSTN participants in one-to-one Teams calls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will support explicit consent for participants connected through the public switched telephone network (PSTN) in one-to-one calls.

claims.claim: When consent is required, the PSTN participant hears an audio prompt when recording or transcription starts.
claims.quote: When explicit consent is required, PSTN participants will hear an audio prompt when recording or transcription is started.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A PSTN participant who declines can remain in the call but stays muted.
claims.quote: PSTN participants who decline can remain in the call but stay muted.

claims.quote: This capability extends the existing Teams calling policy for explicit consent to one-to-one PSTN calls.

claims.claim: PSTN participants press 1 to consent.
claims.quote: Participants can press 1 to consent or 2 to decline.

claims.claim: PSTN participants press 2 to decline.
claims.quote: Participants can press 1 to consent or 2 to decline.

claims.claim: The PSTN participant's audio is excluded from recording and transcription before consent.
claims.quote: The PSTN participant's audio will not be included in the recording or transcript before consent is provided.

claims.claim: The cited consent-setting path is Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Insert Edit after policy in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered row: Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription. The cited page explicitly requires Edit after selecting the policy.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams module provides Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent <string> to modify calling-policy consent.
claims.quote: [-Identity] <string> [...] [-ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>]. This feature has not been released yet and will have no changes if it is enabled or disabled.
claims.fix: Keep the command, but add that the cmdlet reference currently marks ExplicitRecordingConsent unreleased and ineffective, while the call-configuration guide and MC1530950 describe the existing policy. Report this documentation discrepancy rather than silently presenting the reference as unqualified confirmation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate PSTN-only or keypad-only consent switch on the admin UI or PowerShell surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN-only keypad-only explicit recording consent Teams admin center PowerShell Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy parameter; read teams-calling-policy, call-recording-transcription-captions, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy and MC1530950.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Cloud recording for calling controls whether a user's one-to-one Teams or PSTN call can be recorded.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy that you want to edit. [...] Turn Cloud recording for calling to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true enables call recording in the global calling policy, rather than controlling consent.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables call recording for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription controls whether users can transcribe one-to-one and PSTN calls.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy you want to modify. [...] Turn Transcription to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables transcription in the global policy, rather than controlling consent.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true

claims.claim: The consent requirement is admin-opt-in through the existing calling-policy setting.
claims.quote: The existing explicit consent setting is disabled by default. [...] If your organization wants to require explicit consent, enable the existing setting in the appropriate calling policies.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing, metering and charges for the new keypad capability are not yet published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN explicit recording consent licensing license meter charge keypad; read MC1530950, call-recording-transcription-captions, teams-recording-policy and Microsoft Teams add-on licenses. No keypad-specific licence, meter or charge stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The supplied notice names no licence, meter or charge for the capability.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete supplied MC1530950 notice, including impact, action recommendations and compliance considerations; it names no licence, meter or charge.

claims.claim: Learn says PSTN call recording policy scope includes users with Microsoft 365 E5, Office 365 E5, or Microsoft/Office 365 E3 with a Teams Phone add-on licence, as general recording context.
claims.quote: In convenience recording, policy scope for calls includes Teams PSTN calls, if the user has one of the following licenses: Microsoft 365 E5, Office 365 E5, or Microsoft/Office 365 E3 with Teams Phone Add-on license.

claims.claim: The call-configuration guide says ExplicitRecordingConsent manages consent for both one-to-one VoIP and PSTN calls.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls.
claims.fix: Keep the attributed statement, but cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/participant-agreement-recording-transcription and note that its endpoint list still places PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls under auto consent, with consent data logged as 'not applicable' or 'auto consent'. Distinguish that existing documentation from the planned keypad update.

claims.claim: Audio Conferencing and group-call recording consent are managed by Teams meeting policy rather than the calling policy.
claims.quote: Audio conferencing and group calls are managed by Teams Meeting Policy.

claims.claim: The call-configuration guide describes a Yes or No consent prompt when a participant tries to unmute, enable their camera or share content.
claims.quote: When a participant decides to un-mute, turn on their camera, or share content, they're asked to respond 'Yes' or 'No' to consent to be included in the recording and transcription.

claims.claim: The cited call-configuration guide does not describe the new one-to-one PSTN keypad prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN one-to-one explicit recording consent keypad PSTN-only setting press 1 2; read call-recording-transcription-captions in full. Its consent section describes Yes/No, not one-to-one PSTN keypad selections.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: With agreement required, the other participant remains muted until agreeing, while the recording or transcription initiator remains unmuted.
claims.quote: The other call participant is muted, with their camera and content-share turned off. The user who initiates recording or transcription is considered to have given consent and remains unmuted.

claims.claim: Learn states that admins can see each call participant's consent choice.
claims.quote: The consent choice for each participant is visible by the admin and is included in the Purview audit log for the call.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn states that each participant's call consent choice is included in the Purview audit log.
claims.quote: The consent choice for each participant is visible by the admin and is included in the Purview audit log for the call.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether the new PSTN keypad choice is audited identically to other call-consent choices.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN keypad consent Purview audit consent sign in permissions call queue; read MC1530950, call-recording-transcription-captions and participant-agreement-recording-transcription excerpts. No new keypad-choice audit mapping stated.

claims.claim: No new identity is involved in the capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams one-to-one PSTN keypad recording consent no new identity permissions sign-in; read MC1530950 and call-recording-transcription-captions. Neither states the blanket no-new-identity claim.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new identity ... is involved'. Retain the documented narrower statement that participants respond using the phone keypad and that the notice describes no sign-in step.

claims.claim: No new permission is involved in the capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams one-to-one PSTN keypad recording consent no new identity permissions sign-in; read MC1530950 and call-recording-transcription-captions. Neither states that no new permission is involved.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that no new permission is involved. Replace the whole opening clause with 'The notice describes participants responding from their phone keypad, without describing a sign-in step.'

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes no sign-in step for the PSTN participant.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1530950 in full; its participant steps are an audio prompt followed by pressing 1 or 2, and it describes no participant sign-in step.

claims.claim: With ExplicitRecordingConsent disabled, users are not required to obtain explicit recording consent.
claims.quote: Disabled: Users are not required to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.

claims.claim: When the calling-policy consent setting is off, external PSTN participants are included in recordings and transcripts that a Teams user starts.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 1:1 PSTN calls ExplicitRecordingConsent Disabled participants included recordings transcripts no consent; read the calling-policy reference and call guide. The explicit all-participants inclusion wording found applies to meetings.
claims.fix: Replace this sentence with 'The calling-policy reference says Disabled does not require users to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.' Do not extend the meeting-policy statement about inclusion in recordings and transcripts to PSTN calls without a stating source.

claims.claim: The feature description documents no autonomous action.
claims.quote: Searched: read the roadmap record, MC1530950 and the call guide; the documented flow starts when recording or transcription is started and requests the participant's response. No autonomous action is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn states that explicit consent is not supported for call queue calls.
claims.quote: Explicit consent is not supported for call queue calls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied notice does not specify whether the new keypad capability changes the existing call queue limitation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN keypad consent Purview audit consent sign in permissions call queue; read MC1530950, the call guide and call queue search excerpts. No keypad-update-specific change to the call queue limitation is stated.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Calling policies are assigned to users, so consent configuration can differ by assigned policy rather than being a separate per-PSTN-call switch.
claims.quote: You can use the global (Org-wide default) policy that's created automatically or create and assign custom policies. [...] You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The new keypad experience affects applicable one-to-one PSTN calls where the existing policy requires consent, rather than calls whose policy leaves consent disabled.
claims.quote: PSTN participants in applicable one-to-one Teams calls where explicit consent for recording or transcription is required

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn directs admins to the Added information about call participants filter in Teams calling audit logs in Purview to view consent data.
claims.quote: You can view consent data using the Added information about call participants filter in the Teams calling audit logs in Purview.

claims.claim: The cited call-configuration guide does not give a full Purview navigation path for viewing call-consent data.
claims.quote: Searched: read call-recording-transcription-captions in full, including View consent data; it names the Purview calling-audit-log filter and links to Audit log activities but supplies no full navigation path itself.

claims.claim: The checklist tells admins to review consent audit data, but the controls table has no consent-audit row.
claims.quote: Use the Added information about call participants filter in the Teams calling audit logs in Purview to review consent data. [The table contains only consent, a PSTN-only switch, recording and transcription rows.]
claims.fix: Add a governance-controls row for reviewing call-consent audit data, naming the documented 'Added information about call participants' filter and citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/call-recording-transcription-captions. Preserve the caveat that keypad-specific audit behaviour is unconfirmed; do not invent navigation or an API.

claims.claim: The notice calls for preparing users and support teams when explicit consent is already enabled, without requiring new configuration when the existing configuration meets organisational requirements.
claims.quote: No new policy configuration is required if your existing explicit consent configuration meets your organization's requirements. [...] If explicit consent is already enabled, prepare users and support teams for the new PSTN keypad consent experience.
